chunks: And I asked him about a man who places a vow upon himself and does not specify it. He said: “If you specified it, then it is what you specified. And if you did not specify anything, then it is nothing. But if you said, ‘For Allah, it is upon me,’ then the expiation is the expiation of an oath.”

key_terms.كَفَّارَةُ: the required expiation for violating or mishandling the obligation
key_terms.لِلَّهِ: for Allah, indicating dedication to Allah
key_terms.نَذْرًا: a vow a person places upon himself for Allah
key_terms.يَمِينٍ: an oath, whose expiation is used here as the legal measure
key_terms.يُسَمِّيهِ: to specify or define the vow explicitly

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on making a vow without specifying what it is?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on an unspecified nadhr. If a person specifies the vow, then he is bound by what he specified; if he leaves it completely unspecified, it carries no binding effect. However, if he says, ‘For Allah, it is upon me,’ then a kaffarah equivalent to the expiation of an oath applies.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
I asked Imam (as) about a man who makes a vow upon himself without specifying it.
Imam (as) said: "If you specify it, then it is as you specified. But if you do not specify anything, then it is of no consequence. However, if you said: 'It is upon me for the sake of Allah (swt),' then its expiation is the expiation of an oath."
